knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly writes the credibility premium with Z and states what Z weights?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Standard form blends individual and collateral means with Z on individual experience. Full credibility always or reversed weights are wrong.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Premium = Z X̄ + (1-Z) mu; Z weights individual experience.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Always taking Z=1 or reversing weights on individual versus collateral.

choices.label: Credibility premium = Z times X̄ + (1 minus Z) times μ, where Z weights the individual experience X̄ versus the collateral or manual mean μ.
Always use full credibility Z = 1 regardless of sample size or data quality.
Z weights the collateral mean only; the individual experience enters with weight (1 minus Z) always.
Credibility premium equals mu alone because collateral information dominates individual experience by definition.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Individual mean claim X̄ = 1200, collateral or manual mean μ = 1000, credibility factor Z = 0.4. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Compute premium; refuse full credibility always.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Arithmetic gives 1080. Z=0.4 on individual experience pulls toward mu. Full credibility or reversed weights misapply the formula.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Always using Z=1 or swapping weights to collateral.

choices.label: Premium = Z times X̄ + (1 minus Z) times μ = 0.4 times 1200 + 0.6 times 1000 = 480 + 600 = 1080. Z is the weight on the individual experience versus the collateral mean. With limited or noisy data, Z less than 1 shrinks toward the collateral or manual mean.
Premium = 1200 because individual experience must always receive full credibility Z = 1.
Premium = 0.4 times 1000 + 0.6 times 1200 = 1120 because Z weights the collateral mean.
Premium = 1000 because collateral mean mu is the credibility premium by definition.

worked_example.title: Credibility premium with given Z
worked_example.problem_statement: A risk's sample mean claim cost is X̄ = £1200. The hypothetical mean for the risk class is μ = £1000. The credibility factor is Z = 0.55. Compute the credibility premium P = Z X̄ + (1 − Z)μ and state what Z weights.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Form the convex combination with weights Z and 1 − Z.

steps.label: Complementary weight
steps.explanation: Credibility premiums are weighted averages of individual and collective means.

steps.label: Credibility premium
steps.explanation: Substitute the given values into the standard credibility formula.

steps.label: Interpret Z
steps.explanation: Z is the weight on the risk's own experience X̄; 1 − Z weights the class hypothetical mean.
steps.calculation: Z weights X̄; (1 − Z) weights μ

worked_example.final_answer: Credibility premium P = £1110; Z = 0.55 weights individual experience.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Swapping the weights so that Z multiplies μ, or treating Z as a probability that must equal X̄/μ.
